tool_input.command: git diff HEAD -- modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/streaming.go modules/caddyhttp/server.go | head -600; git status --short | head -30

structured_output.summary: I found nothing that blocks the change. My probe covers the Caddyfile and registry paths (ACC9, ACC10 and the upstream-removal part of ACC2) and passes. I reviewed the remaining criteria by reading the code and tests, not by probing them. The implementation matches the criteria, and the integration tests use real servers and clients. One unprobed gap: intercept.go is declared for this task but not modified, and I didn't check that intercept's recorder path is guarded.

findings.text: Detached streams to dynamic upstreams are keyed by an empty upstream string and never closed on removal, and no test covers that case or stream_timeout combined with detached; the first is documented in the field comment.
StreamLogs.skipHandshake() and the nil-receiver handling are thin wrappers that could be inlined.

coverage.note: Echoes through two reloads and a new stream afterwards.
Checks that the removed stream closes and the retained one keeps echoing, including after a further reload.
Covers both the no-delay and the 3s-delay cases, and checks that the elapsed time is at least 2s.
Counts the 101 entries in the access log for the default, level-only and skip_handshake configs.
Checks the default DEBUG level (not logged at INFO), a configured level, the logger name and the byte counts.
The recorder is tested directly; the encode writer is only exercised in the integration test.
Runs a plain echo upgrade and a WebSocket upgrade through encode and intercept with handle_response, and checks the access log.
The h2 case is TestExtendedConnectH2, which runs in a child process with GODEBUG set and is skipped under -short.
Forty concurrent finish and markResult calls produce exactly one accounting, with the byte counts checked.
A table test over valid and invalid inputs, plus the adapt test.
